questions.explain: Change Tracking records per-table primary keys of changed rows plus the change version — not the data itself — keeping overhead minimal; TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED records which columns changed for column-aware triggers.

questions.explain: The cursor is persisted per trigger in change_cursors; the worker checks CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION — if the cursor is older than retention, it must resynchronize (full sweep) rather than resume blindly.
options: Cursors are kept in memory only
Poll as fast as possible with no cursor
Persist the version cursor per trigger and guard with CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION, resyncing on retention expiry
Retention expiry is harmless

questions.explain: Reactions enqueue work (ingest queue, agent runs, quota procedures) rather than doing it inline — the poll loop stays fast and transactional; the fan-out mapping lives in a table so reactions can be toggled without deployments.
options: Do all work inline in the poll loop
Reactions enqueue work; they don't do it — fan-out via a toggleable table mapping
Polling loops should be slow
One reaction per database maximum
questions.q: What is the "reactions enqueue work" principle?

questions.explain: Column-aware reaction: only re-embed when the content column actually changed (SYS_CHANGE_COLUMNS bitmask check) — metadata edits don't waste embedding API budget.
options: Re-embed on every update
Never re-embed
Re-embed on a fixed schedule
Re-embed only when the content column changed, using the SYS_CHANGE_COLUMNS bitmask
questions.q: How do you avoid wasting embedding budget on irrelevant updates?

questions.explain: Change Tracking answers 'which rows changed' (reaction re-reads the current row); CDC answers 'what did rows look like before/after' (audit diffs, delta pipelines) — enable both where both questions matter.
options: 'Which rows changed' → Change Tracking; 'before/after images' → CDC
They are interchangeable
Always use CDC for triggers
Always use Change Tracking for auditing
